plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet mandate limits.
Trim SPY to 15% to further reduce overall market exposure.
This strategy prioritizes capital preservation and low drawdown.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation, targeting around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering overall concentration. Expect lower volatility but also more modest returns.

plan: For risk-first growth, trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 1%, MUU to 1%, PLTU to 1%, and METU to 3%.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet mandate limits.
Buy SPXS at 4% to add some inverse market exposure for balance.
This plan blends broad index, quality tech, and a small amount of leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a small inverse position for hedging. Expect moderate returns with controlled risk.

moves.note: Add inverse semis for aggressive hedge

plan: For aggressive growth, add to SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, and METU, targeting 6% each.
Trim QQQI to 15% to make room for increased leveraged exposure.
Buy SOXS at 5% to add an aggressive inverse semiconductor hedge.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for higher potential returns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs, which amplifies both upside and drawdown. Be aware of daily decay and the potential for rapid losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

moves.note: Reduce broad index for income focus

plan: To park cash for yield, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU) to zero.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30% for increased income generation.
Trim SPY to 10% to further shift focus towards income-generating assets.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on steady distributions. It minimizes exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets, favoring income-generating ETFs. While aiming for reliable income, remember distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
